defaults.permitted_development: Demolition in England is controlled by the GPDO and heritage legislation, not treated as a free general right. The route depends on what is being removed, whether Part 11 prior approval applies, and whether the site is listed, in a conservation area or otherwise protected. The route often turns on heritage status, neighbour safety and whether the work is standalone demolition or part of a wider redevelopment.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height allowance. The real question is the size, type and status of the structure and whether its removal falls within a prior approval route or needs a fuller application.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate depth rule. Partial demolition, demolition linked to rebuilding, or removal of only part of a structure must be assessed against the actual scope of works and any related development.
rules.boundary_rules: Party walls, adjoining land, hoardings, highway occupation, neighbour safety and the stability of nearby structures are often the most important boundary and site-management issues in a demolition proposal. The route often turns on heritage status, neighbour safety and whether the work is standalone demolition or part of a wider redevelopment.
rules.roof_rules: Removing a roof is not automatically a standalone permitted step. Once roof removal forms part of wider demolition, heritage, structural and weatherproofing issues can change the planning route.
rules.materials_rules: Salvage, asbestos handling, waste removal and making good exposed surfaces are key practical issues. Separate environmental, safety and building-control duties still apply even where the planning route is clear. The route often turns on heritage status, neighbour safety and whether the work is standalone demolition or part of a wider redevelopment.

rules.permitted_development: In Broxbourne, the route depends on the structure, its heritage status and any prior approval step; clearance beside occupied housing usually turns on safe sequencing and the treatment of the cleared plot.

rules.height_rules: In Broxbourne, once demolition involves tall retained walls, chimneys or prominent temporary works, the safety and neighbour impact case becomes much tighter than the drawings may suggest.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate depth rule. Partial demolition, demolition tied to rebuilding, or removal of only part of a structure must be judged on the actual scope of works and any linked development.
rules.boundary_rules: In Broxbourne, boundaries are usually tested by access for plant, neighbour safety, hoarding lines and what happens where garages, fences or attached structures meet the demolition edge.
rules.roof_rules: Taking off a roof is not automatically a standalone permitted step. Where roof removal forms part of wider demolition, heritage, structural and weatherproofing issues can change the planning route.
rules.materials_rules: Salvage, recycling, asbestos handling, waste removal and making good exposed surfaces are key practical issues. Separate environmental and building-control duties still apply even where the planning route is clear. The route often turns on heritage status, neighbour safety and whether the work is standalone demolition or part of a wider redevelopment.

restrictions.conservation_area: Demolition in a conservation area can need planning permission for relevant demolition and a much closer heritage review, even where the structure looks minor.
restrictions.listed_building: Demolition of a listed building, or of a curtilage structure protected as part of it, needs listed building consent.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can remove fallback demolition rights in selected locations, so check the site's designation before assuming a prior approval or permitted route still applies.
